faults.fault: On widening (image 3) the fixed-size backglass art leaves tall dark blank filler bands on either side of the PINBALL art inside the backbox face. The backbox front reads as a picture with dead panels bolted beside it rather than a wider backbox — the ends should carry the art/frame, not bare smeared dark texture.
In the widened render the speaker panel's end extensions show stretched streaky texture around the spread speaker circles rather than clean grille, readable as a smear a player could point at.
Solid blue geometry fills the void beneath the front legs down to the floor instead of remaining open air.
Severe geometry shearing and tearing opens visible gaps through the cabinet when scaled vertically.
Vertical seam and texture disruption down the center of the backbox art during horizontal scaling.

wider_means: A wider pinball is a wider cabinet with a wider playfield -- same parts, just a broader body and longer cross-members.
taller_means: A taller pinball has a deeper-standing cabinet: a longer plain lower body panel and longer legs, with the backbox unchanged.

faults.fault: When widened, the backglass art tiles instead of staying one piece: the PINBALL marquee reads 'P PINBALL L' with cut and duplicated letters at both edges. Text is doubled and cut -- blocking.

When made taller, the cabinet front panel detaches from the body: it leans outward past the legs, the playfield opening gaps open, and the legs are left floating clear of the cabinet. The whole silhouette no longer reads as a pinball cabinet -- blocking.
In the taller render the background panel balloons forward and swallows the cabinet, presenting a blank smeared blue slab across the front of the prop -- looks like a bug, not a decision -- blocking.
Text repeats and clips at wide aspect ratios.
Vertical scaling severely distorts geometry, creating an extruded ramp and disconnecting the lower cabinet.
Solid blue extrusion fills the open space beneath the coin door between front legs.
